title: Reverse diffusion process
reading: The slide introduces the reverse (generative) direction of diffusion models: a neural network denoiser is trained to undo the noising process, mapping noise back to data. A filmstrip figure plus a zoomed single-step inset illustrate the idea, and a red annotation frames each denoising step as supervised learning.

visuals.description: Horizontal strip of pixelated images from pure colour noise labelled x_T on the left to a clean sprite-like image x_0 on the right, with an arrow labelled 'Reverse diffusion process'. Below, a zoom shows x_t passed through a block arrow labelled f_theta producing x_{t-1}.
visuals.assertion: Generation proceeds by repeatedly applying a learned denoiser f_theta that maps x_t to a slightly less noisy x_{t-1}, from x_T down to x_0.

concepts.name: Reverse diffusion / denoiser network
concepts.why_it_matters: It is the learned generative component of diffusion models.

concepts.name: Supervised learning per step
concepts.why_it_matters: Each denoising step has a known target, making training tractable.

verbatim_spans: Diffusion models then train a neural network (denoiser) to reverse this process
Each step is a supervised learning process!
